questions.q: Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} x & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$. If $ABA^t = [-20]$ then the value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
$A = \begin{bmatrix} x & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$

$B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} x & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} x(1) + 1(4) - 2(7) & x(2) + 1(5) - 2(8) & x(3) + 1(6) - 2(9) \end{bmatrix}$

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} x - 10 & 2x - 11 & 3x - 12 \end{bmatrix}$

$ABA^t = \begin{bmatrix} x - 10 & 2x - 11 & 3x - 12 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}$

$ABA^t = [x(x - 10) + 1(2x - 11) - 2(3x - 12)]$

$ABA^t = [x^2 - 10x + 2x - 11 - 6x + 24]$

$ABA^t = [x^2 - 14x + 13]$

Given $ABA^t = [-20]$, we have:

$x^2 - 14x + 13 = -20$

$x^2 - 14x + 33 = 0$

$(x - 3)(x - 11) = 0$

$x = 3$ or $x = 11$

From the given options, $x = 11$.

Answer: $11$

questions.q: If the matrix $M = \begin{bmatrix} x+5 & a & -4 \\ -2 & 0 & b \\ c & 6 & y+1 \end{bmatrix}$ is a skew symmetric matrix, the value of the expression $ab + c^2 - xy$ is:
questions.solution:
For a skew-symmetric matrix $M$, $M^T = -M$.

The diagonal elements must be zero:
$x + 5 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -5$
$y + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow y = -1$

For non-diagonal elements, $m_{ij} = -m_{ji}$:
$m_{12} = -m_{21} \Rightarrow a = -(-2) = 2$
$m_{13} = -m_{31} \Rightarrow -4 = -c \Rightarrow c = 4$
$m_{23} = -m_{32} \Rightarrow b = -6$

Substituting these values into the expression $ab + c^2 - xy$:
$ab + c^2 - xy = (2)(-6) + (4)^2 - (-5)(-1)$
$= -12 + 16 - 5$
$= -1$

Answer: $-1$

questions.q:
Matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$,
Given $M_{22}$ and $A_{32}$ are the minor and cofactor of the adjoint matrix of A respectively then the value of the expression $M_{22} + A_{32} - |adj\ A|$ is:
questions.solution:
The given matrix is $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$.

First, we find the determinant of matrix $A$:
$|A| = 1((-2)(-1) - (2)(0)) - 1((1)(-1) - (2)(1)) + 2((1)(0) - (-2)(1))$
$|A| = 1(2) - 1(-3) + 2(2) = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9$

Using the property of the adjoint of a matrix, $|adj\ A| = |A|^{n-1}$. For a $3 \times 3$ matrix, $n = 3$:
$|adj\ A| = |A|^{3-1} = 9^2 = 81$

Let $B = adj\ A$. We need to find the minor $M_{22}$ and cofactor $A_{32}$ of matrix $B$.
Let $C$ be the cofactor matrix of $B$. By definition, $adj\ B = C^T$, which implies $C = (adj\ B)^T$.

Using the property $adj(adj\ A) = |A|^{n-2}A$, for $n=3$, we have:
$adj\ B = adj(adj\ A) = |A|^{3-2}A = 9A$

Therefore, the cofactor matrix of $B$ is:
$C = (9A)^T = 9A^T$

The cofactor of the $(3,2)$ element of $B$ is $A_{32}$, which is simply $C_{32}$:
$A_{32} = C_{32} = 9(A^T)_{32} = 9A_{23}$
From matrix $A$, the element $A_{23} = 2$.
$A_{32} = 9(2) = 18$

The minor of the $(2,2)$ element of $B$ is $M_{22}$. Since $C_{22} = (-1)^{2+2}M_{22} = M_{22}$, we have:
$M_{22} = C_{22} = 9(A^T)_{22} = 9A_{22}$
From matrix $A$, the element $A_{22} = -2$.
$M_{22} = 9(-2) = -18$

Finally, we evaluate the given expression:
$M_{22} + A_{32} - |adj\ A| = -18 + 18 - 81 = -81$

Answer: $-81$

questions.q: If A and B are two square matrices of the same order such that $AB = A$ and $BA = B$, then $(A + B)^2$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given $AB = A$ and $BA = B$.

We can find $A^2$ and $B^2$ as follows:
$A^2 = A \cdot A = (AB)A = A(BA)$
Substituting $BA = B$, we get:
$A^2 = AB = A$

Similarly, for $B^2$:
$B^2 = B \cdot B = (BA)B = B(AB)$
Substituting $AB = A$, we get:
$B^2 = BA = B$

Now, expanding $(A + B)^2$:
$(A + B)^2 = (A + B)(A + B)$
$(A + B)^2 = A^2 + AB + BA + B^2$

Substituting $A^2 = A$, $B^2 = B$, $AB = A$, and $BA = B$ into the expansion:
$(A + B)^2 = A + A + B + B$
$(A + B)^2 = 2A + 2B = 2(A + B)$

Answer: $2(A + B)$

questions.q: Given the matrices $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, then the minor $M_{23}$ of the matrix $(A B^{-1})^{-1}$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $C = (A B^{-1})^{-1}$. Using the reversal law for matrix inverses, we have:

$C = (B^{-1})^{-1} A^{-1} = B A^{-1}$

First, we find the inverse of matrix $A$. The determinant of $A$ is:

$|A| = 1(2 - 0) - 0 + 1(0 - 1) = 1$

The adjugate matrix of $A$ is the transpose of its cofactor matrix. Since $A$ is symmetric, $\text{adj}(A)$ is also symmetric:

$\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

Thus, $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|} \text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

Now, we compute $C = B A^{-1}$:

$C = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

We only need the elements of the 1st and 3rd rows of $C$ to find the minor $M_{23}$ (which is obtained by deleting the 2nd row and 3rd column):

$c_{11} = (2)(2) + (1)(0) + (0)(-1) = 4$

$c_{12} = (2)(0) + (1)(1) + (0)(0) = 1$

$c_{31} = (0)(2) + (2)(0) + (1)(-1) = -1$

$c_{32} = (0)(0) + (2)(1) + (1)(0) = 2$

The minor $M_{23}$ is the determinant of the $2 \times 2$ submatrix formed by these elements:

$M_{23} = \begin{vmatrix} c_{11} \text{ and } c_{12} \\ c_{31} \text{ and } c_{32} \end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix} 4 \text{ and } 1 \\ -1 \text{ and } 2 \end{vmatrix}$

$M_{23} = (4)(2) - (1)(-1) = 8 + 1 = 9$

Answer: $9$

questions.q: Given $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$ and $f(x) = x^2 - 2x - 3$ then $f(A)$ is:
questions.solution:
Given $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\\\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$ and $f(x) = x^2 - 2x - 3$

$f(A) = A^2 - 2A - 3I$

$A^2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\\\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\\\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 8 \\\\ 8 & 13 \end{pmatrix}$

$f(A) = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 8 \\\\ 8 & 13 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 4 \\\\ 4 & 6 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 \\\\ 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$

$f(A) = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 4 \\\\ 4 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$

Since $(f(A))^T = f(A)$, the resulting matrix is a symmetric matrix.

Answer: Symmetric Matrix

questions.q: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{lll}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]$ and I is an identity by matrix of order $3 \times 3$ then $A(\operatorname{adj} A)=$
questions.solution:
The property of the adjoint of a matrix states that $A(\operatorname{adj} A) = |A| I$, where $|A|$ is the determinant of matrix $A$ and $I$ is the identity matrix of the same order.

Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$, we calculate the determinant $|A|$ by expanding along the first row:

$|A| = 2(1 \times 3 - 2 \times 2) - 1(3 \times 3 - 2 \times 1) + 3(3 \times 2 - 1 \times 1)$

$|A| = 2(3 - 4) - 1(9 - 2) + 3(6 - 1)$

$|A| = 2(-1) - 1(7) + 3(5)$

$|A| = -2 - 7 + 15 = 6$

Therefore, $A(\operatorname{adj} A) = 6I$.

Answer: 6 I

questions.q: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{rr}\cos \dfrac{2 \pi}{3} & -\sin \dfrac{2 \pi}{3} \\ \sin \dfrac{2 \pi}{3} & \cos \dfrac{2 \pi}{3}\end{array}\right]$ and I is an identity matrix of order $2 \times 2$ then $A^3=$
questions.solution:
The matrix $A$ is given by $A = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \dfrac{2 \pi}{3} & -\sin \dfrac{2 \pi}{3} \\ \sin \dfrac{2 \pi}{3} & \cos \dfrac{2 \pi}{3} \end{bmatrix}$.

This is a rotation matrix of the form $R(\theta) = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & -\sin \theta \\ \sin \theta & \cos \theta \end{bmatrix}$ where $\theta = \dfrac{2 \pi}{3}$.

The property of rotation matrices states that $R(\theta)^n = R(n \theta)$.

Therefore, $A^3 = R\left(3 \times \dfrac{2 \pi}{3}\right) = R(2 \pi)$.

Calculating the values for $R(2 \pi)$: $R(2 \pi) = \begin{bmatrix} \cos(2 \pi) & -\sin(2 \pi) \\ \sin(2 \pi) & \cos(2 \pi) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

Since $\begin{bmatrix}$1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = I$, it follows that $A^3 = I$.

Answer: I$

Given the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -3 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

The transpose of matrix $A$ is $A^T = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

Observe that $A^T = -A$, which implies that $A$ is a skew-symmetric matrix.

We need to compute $A + 2A^T$.

Substituting $A^T = -A$ into the expression, we get $A + 2(-A) = A - 2A = -A$.

Since $A^T = -A$, it follows that $-A = A^T$.

Therefore, $A + 2A^T = A^T$.

Answer: $A^T$

questions.solution:

questions.solution:
A matrix $A$ is invertible if and only if its determinant is non-zero, i.e., $|A| eq 0$.

The determinant of matrix $A = egin{bmatrix} 4 & \lambda & -3 \ 0 & 2 & 5 \ 1 & 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ is calculated by expanding along the first column:

$|A| = 4(2 imes 3 - 5 imes 1) - 0(\lambda imes 3 - (-3) imes 1) + 1(\lambda imes 5 - (-3) imes 2)$

$|A| = 4(6 - 5) - 0 + 1(5\lambda + 6)$

$|A| = 4(1) + 5\lambda + 6 = 5\lambda + 10$

For $A^{-1}$ to exist, $|A| eq 0$.

$5\lambda + 10 eq 0$

$5\lambda eq -10$

$\lambda eq -2$

Answer: $\lambda eq-2$

questions.solution:
Given $X = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $Y = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

Calculate $X \cos \theta + Y \sin \theta$:

$X \cos \theta = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & 0 \\ 0 & \cos \theta \end{bmatrix}$

$Y \sin \theta = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \sin \theta \\ -\sin \theta & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

Adding these two matrices:

$X \cos \theta + Y \sin \theta = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & 0 \\ 0 & \cos \theta \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \sin \theta \\ -\sin \theta & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & \sin \theta \\ -\sin \theta & \cos \theta \end{bmatrix}$

This result is identical to the given matrix $B$.

Answer: $X \cos \theta+Y \sin \theta$

questions.solution:
Given $A(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \cos t & \sin t \\ -\sin t & \cos t \end{bmatrix}$.

Then $A(-t) = \begin{bmatrix} \cos(-t) & \sin(-t) \\ -\sin(-t) & \cos(-t) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos t & -\sin t \\ \sin t & \cos t \end{bmatrix}$.

The product $A(t)A(-t)$ is calculated as:

$\begin{bmatrix} \cos t & \sin t \\ -\sin t & \cos t \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \cos t & -\sin t \\ \sin t & \cos t \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos^2 t + \sin^2 t & -\cos t \sin t + \sin t \cos t \\ -\sin t \cos t + \cos t \sin t & \sin^2 t + \cos^2 t \end{bmatrix}$.

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1$, we get:

$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = I$.

Thus, the product is the identity matrix.

Answer: Identity matrix

questions.q: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{cc}1 & -2 \\ 4 & 5\end{array}\right] ; f(t)=t^2-3 t+7$ then $f(A)+\left[\begin{array}{cc}3 & 6 \\ -12 & -9\end{array}\right]=$
questions.solution:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$ and $f(t) = t^2 - 3t + 7$.

First, calculate $A^2$:
$A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1(1) + (-2)(4) & 1(-2) + (-2)(5) \\ 4(1) + 5(4) & 4(-2) + 5(5) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -7 & -12 \\ 24 & 17 \end{bmatrix}$

Next, calculate $f(A) = A^2 - 3A + 7I$:
$f(A) = \begin{bmatrix} -7 & -12 \\ 24 & 17 \end{bmatrix} - 3 \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix} + 7 \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$
$f(A) = \begin{bmatrix} -7 & -12 \\ 24 & 17 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -6 \\ 12 & 15 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 0 \\ 0 & 7 \end{bmatrix}$
$f(A) = \begin{bmatrix} -7 - 3 + 7 & -12 + 6 + 0 \\ 24 - 12 + 0 & 17 - 15 + 7 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & -6 \\ 12 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

Finally, add the given matrix to $f(A)$:
$f(A) + \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 \\ -12 & -9 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & -6 \\ 12 & 9 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 \\ -12 & -9 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

Answer: $\left[\begin{array}{ll}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{array}\right]$

Comparing $P^6 = 5I - 8P$ with the given equation $P^n = 5I - 8P$, we find $n = 6$.

Thus, $A^n = 2^{n-1} A$ for $n \ge 1$.

Substituting $n+1$ for $n$, we get $A^{n+1} = 2^{(n+1)-1} A = 2^n A$.

Therefore, $A^{n+1} = 2^n \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.
